messages:
Anya: Quick thread — since the v3 FlashAttention RFC merged, perf on ded-rt has stable throughput but we're seeing p99 spikes (~2.8x) for short-sequence, small-batch traffic (seq<=32, batch 1-4) on A100s. Anyone else? :thinking:
Mike: saw that too, added sampling on prod. spikes line up with allocator churn when KV cache hit rate is low.
Suyog: can you paste the sample shapes / job ids?
Anya: shapes: mostly (1,16), (4,32). p50 unchanged, p95 fine, p99 up from ~80ms -> ~240ms. Reproducer: `python -m repro.flashattn_shortseq --model redwood/vicuna-13b --seq 16 --batch 2`
Olivia: interesting — on hetero pools we mix bf16+fp16 allocations. flashattn-v3 uses a workspace-size heuristic that assumes contiguous free region; fragmentation causes fallback kernel which is slower because it triggers small-block mallocs per request.
Mike: telemetry shows >30% of shortseq requests hit fallback kernel because workspace_alloc failed and we reallocate per-call.
DeployBot: deploy 2432109800 merged: "fa3-v3-kernel-selection" (prod rollout 5%).
Suyog: can you paste allocator logs snippet?
Anya: logs:
```
[alloc] try_reserve(1048576) -> fail (largest_free=262144)
[alloc] fallback -> allocate_scratch(128K) per request
[kernel] selected=flashattn_v3_fast, fallback=flashattn_generic
```
Mike: note flashattn_v3_fast expects contiguous workspace ~1MB for multi-head fprop. For seq<=32 it's overprovisioned; v3's new workspace packing made it worse for tiny seq because coalescing is less effective.
Olivia: hypothesis: our kernel-selection heuristic is too aggressive — prefers fast kernel for shapes where it only wins when workspace is contiguous. For fragmented memory it falls back late.
Anya: proposed fixes:
- change heuristic to prefer generic kernel when seq<40 and batch<4 unless continuous_free_space >= threshold
- add `workspace_probe` telemetry: sample 1% of requests to try reserving workspace and record largest_free before selection
- allocator: try a best-fit-with-defrag path on idle GPU cycles
- canary rollout plan
Mike: agree. Also add metric: `kernel_fallback_rate_by_shape` and `alloc_fail_reason`.
Suyog: implementation notes: cheapest is heuristic tweak + metrics. Defrag is bigger (needs cudaSync+pauses). Might be ok as opt-in.
Olivia: I'll open a PR with metric names + heuristic change. Can we also add a small microbench in runtime-tests for (1,8) (4,16) shapes to catch regressions in CI?
Anya: yes — add a test that asserts p99 < X for those shapes on a reference perf harness (non-gpu-local can simulate via mocked allocator).
Mike: for rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with watch on p99 spike and kernel_fallback_rate. If fallback_rate doesn't drop, rollback.
Anya: thanks. Can someone pair on the telemetry schema? Need it in console so SRE can alert.
Olivia: I'll draft schema in the PR. Adding fields: shape, batch, seq, largest_free_before_alloc, selected_kernel, fallback_kernel, alloc_fail_reason, timestamp.
Suyog: small nit: keep `largest_free_before_alloc` in bytes; limit sample size to 1% to avoid extra syscalls.
Mike: ack.
Anya: created issue RW-1302 to track. Linking here: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RW-1302
DeployBot: note: alert rule "fa3-kernel-p99-regression" created with threshold 1.5x baseline.
Lee: quick question — does this interact with kv-cache warmstart? we saw worse when cache flushes happened.
Olivia: yes, cache flush increases alloc churn. add a correlator tag `kv_cache_flush` to telemetry.
Anya: ok next steps: Olivia PR heuristic+metrics, Mike add alert thresholds & dashboards, Suyog to prototype defrag path (opt-in) and perf test, Anya to monitor canary. Meeting if needed tomorrow 11:30am.
Mike: :thumbsup:
Anya: thanks all, will update RW-1302 with links.
